failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Which member of Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me" and when did it air?' - This is a natural-language yes/no style question bundling multiple targets (which member + when aired) rather than a targeted entity retrieval query.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Which member of Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me" and when did it air?' and Hop 3 query: 'Which member of the Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me"?' - Both queries ask essentially the same question about which Likwit Crew member hosted the show, with only minor wording changes. Neither query advances the search strategy despite both summaries indicating the show name itself is not found.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 explicitly names the missing evidence: 'Missing critical information: - An evidence document identifying which member of Likwit Crew (Evidence, J-Ro, E-Swift, The Alchemist, or DJ Babu) hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me" - A passage about the MTV show "You Can't See Me" itself, confirming its existence and who hosted it'. Hop 2 query targets this: 'Which member of Likwit Crew hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me"'. Despite three retrieval hops with well-formed queries targeting the missing show, no passage about 'You Can't See Me' as an MTV show ever appears in any retrieval results.
